Native IAAFT surrogate test of an explicitly declared Lyapunov statistic

etr_surrogate_nonlinearity_test.Rd

Independent base-R iterative amplitude-adjusted Fourier-transform surrogates with explicit Rosenstein sample-index statistic and plus-one Monte Carlo tail probability. Published Python 1.2 is the source of the mathematical contract; random draws are not identical across R and NumPy.

Usage

etr_surrogate_nonlinearity_test(trajectories, curve, dimension, statistic,
  embedding_dimension, delay, theiler_window, max_horizon, fit_start, fit_end,
  delay_units = "samples", theiler_window_units = "samples",
  max_horizon_units = "samples", fit_units = "samples", method = "iaaft",
  n_surrogates = 199L, alternative = "greater", max_iterations = 1000L,
  tolerance = 1e-8, random_state = NULL)

Arguments

trajectories

A complete native common-grid trajectory set.

curve

Exact source curve ID or zero-based index.

dimension

An explicitly declared source dimension.

statistic

Only largest_lyapunov is supported.

embedding_dimension

Number of delay-coordinate blocks, at least two.

delay

Positive integer observed-sample delay.

theiler_window

Nonnegative sample-unit neighbor exclusion.

max_horizon

Positive integer forward sample horizon.

fit_start,fit_end

Explicit inclusive fit horizon indices.

delay_units,theiler_window_units,max_horizon_units,fit_units

All must be samples; time conversions are not silently approximated.

method

Only iaaft is supported.

n_surrogates

Positive count of independent IAAFT surrogate series.

alternative

greater, less, or two-sided.

max_iterations

Positive IAAFT convergence iteration limit.

tolerance

Positive finite spectral-error-change stopping threshold.

random_state

Optional scoped base-R nonnegative integer random seed; omitted draws use current R RNG.

Value

A native structured result with observed exponent, per-surrogate exponents, p-value, convergence iterations, spectral errors and fail-closed provenance.

Details

IAAFT preserves each observed finite sample value exactly but approximately matches Fourier amplitude spectrum. The native test uses a plus-one tail probability, doubles the smaller tail for two-sided alternatives and raises an error if a declared surrogate fails to converge. R and NumPy RNG streams are not equivalent. The test is evidence against the declared linear-stochastic null, not proof of a unique deterministic chaotic mechanism or causality. Exact source API parity and sampling calibration have not been certified.
